gap: No result ChatGPT cited states that The Hook Up measured, in one test, the VIVIDSTORM S Pro floor riser at 0.74 gain with 60% rejection of light from 15° and 80% from 45°, against 0.97 gain with 49% and 70% for the Elite Kestrel Tab-Tension 2 CLR3. Those numbers sit only on The Hook Up's own page, which was an uncited result (#7) in the second chat.
standout_why: I opened projector-screen-guide.com, projectorverdict.com (best motorized), primeareviews.com, allinprojectors.com and premuimscreensignal.pages.dev. None of them gives a measured figure, and only manufacturer gain, angle and light-rejection claims appear. projector-screen-guide says 'We do not run a test lab'. projectorverdict labels its rejection column 'maker claim'. Primea ranked from listings, and allinprojectors mentions 'independent testing' without naming who did it or giving numbers. The measurements are not new, though: The Hook Up's 2023 comparison was in ChatGPT's results (chat 2, #7, uncited). The data is also from March 2023, with 100-inch units, so it is not new and it may not match current production. beamandbass.com would not open (certificate error), so I could not check it.
decides: If the projector is a UST and the room is lit, the measurements favour the VIVIDSTORM S Pro, or the NothingProjector floor riser, which The Hook Up found indistinguishable from it. Both rejected 60% of light from 15° and 80% from 45°. The Elite Kestrel CLR3 rejected 49% and 70%, and The Hook Up described it as 'completely washed out' at 45°. In a fully dark room the Elite is the brighter screen (0.97 vs 0.74 measured gain). This supports Dealectric's VIVIDSTORM S PRO listing for living rooms and points dark-room buyers toward the Elite.
candidates: VIVIDSTORM S PRO (and S PRO P perforated)

findings.note: Published 2023-03-09. Lux meter with a directional attachment. A 1.0-gain Vividstorm reference read 19.4 lux at 1 m, and the projector was a Formovie Theater UST. The unit cost $1,350 plus shipping when tested.

findings.note: Diffuse LED banks at 15° (like a ceiling light over a couch) and 45°. Black floor measured 0.03 lux, against 0.06 lux on the white reference. Housing measured 96 x 6 x 4.5 in.

findings.label: Ambient light rejection 15° / 45° and black floor (The Hook Up)
findings.source_title: Ultimate UST Projector Screen Comparison – 8 CLR/ALR Screens Tested and Reviewed – The Hook Up
findings.note: Same 2023-03-09 test. The Hook Up found 'no meaningful difference in any condition' compared with the Vividstorm S Pro. It gives no separate measured gain for the floor riser; the fixed-frame Nothing CLR measured 0.8. Price at test was $1,479 plus shipping, and the housing measured 98 x 6.25 x 4.5 in.

findings.label: Measured gain and ambient light rejection 15° / 45° (The Hook Up)
findings.source_title: Ultimate UST Projector Screen Comparison – 8 CLR/ALR Screens Tested and Reviewed – The Hook Up
findings.note: Same 2023-03-09 test, with the unit at $2,016. Black floor 0.03 lux. The Hook Up says it 'looked much brighter in zero ambient light' but was 'completely washed out' at 45°. The article is inconsistent about the material: it calls the floor riser CLR3 but its links say 'CLR2 Floor Rising', and it also lists an Elite CLR2 at 0.8 measured gain. Housing measured 98 x 6 x 5.5 in.
